title: Proper Positioning and Restraint of a Rat Hind Limb for Focused High Resolution Imaging of Bone Micro-architecture Using In Vivo Micro-computed Tomography
protocol: Prepare the acrylic glass incubation chamber with high-quality O2 at a continuous flow rate of approximately 1-2 L/min.
Transfer the rat to the incubation chamber tail first and close the lid to create an airtight seal.
Begin filling the chamber with veterinary-grade isoflurane at 3-4% v/v dissolved in O2 at a continuous flow rate of 1-2 L/min.
When the rat can no longer stand, transfer it to a face mask or nose cone receiving 1-3% isoflurane dissolved in O2 at a flow rate of 1-2 L/min.
Apply ophthalmic lubrication without antibiotic to protect the delicate membranes of the eyes.
Measure palpebral reflex by gently stimulating palpebral opening.
Measure pedal reflex by pinching hind limbs.
Monitor anesthesia depth until both palpebral and pedal reflexes are absent.
Maintain rat on 0.5-2% isoflurane dissolved in O2 at a flow rate of 1-2 L/min.
Continuously monitor breathing rate throughout the procedure.
Position rat in supine position on carbon-fiber scanner bed.
Restrain right foot in malleable, foam tube with toes extending out.
Apply dental wax to hold foot tightly within foam.
Tape foam tube closed tightly.
Ensure diameter of foam tube fits firmly into plastic tube.
Slide plastic tube into X-ray scanner bed.
Extend rat hind limb until it is taut.
Do not over-extend leg to avoid causing harm.
Pull the left leg along with the tail out of the scanning field of view and toward the torso.
Secure the left leg and the tail in position using masking tape.
Secure the rat body into position at the hips, shoulders, and head with masking tape.
Blot the adhesive side of the masking tape to remove its ability to stick to the rat fur.
Secure the face mask or nose cone to the rat.
Wrap the rat in vet-wrap to limit heat loss.
Continuously monitor the breathing rate of the rat throughout the procedure.
Stop the flow of isoflurane to the rat but maintain a 1-2 L/min flow of O2.
Remove the rat from the respirator when it regains motor control (1-2 min).
Place the rat in a cage on a general-purpose heating pad at low heat for recovery.
Do not leave the rat unattended until it can maintain sternal recumbency.
Ensure food and water are available to the rat during recovery.
